nodes.summary: Stand up the Python project tree, environment, test runner, and Flask application factory.
nodes.instructions:
Create pyproject.toml with a committed uv.lock, a .venv created by uv venv, and app_server/__init__.py exposing create_app() -> Flask.
Add app_server/testing.py exposing web_client() exactly as the Foundation Contract shows.
Register no routes here; the application factory only wires the blueprints and error handlers that later stories add.
nodes.name: Stand up the Python project tree, environment, test runner, and Flask application factory.

nodes.summary: Declare the reading-list store and generate the persistence package from DATABASE.md.
nodes.instructions:
Declare one table, books, with integer primary key, title, author, and insertion ordering by id.
Declare access patterns for create, list in insertion order, get by id, and delete by id.
Drydock generates persistence/ and schema.sql; do not write SQL or sqlite3 calls by hand.
nodes.name: Declare the reading-list store and generate the persistence package from DATABASE.md.

nodes.summary: Accept a title and author, store the book, and reject empty fields with a named reason.
nodes.instructions:
Add the POST /books route. A valid title and author are stored through books.create and the book is returned.
An empty or whitespace-only title or author is rejected with status 400 and a body naming the failing field (title or author), per AC-001.
Pytest covers the add behavior and the rejection behavior.
nodes.name: Accept a title and author, store the book, and reject empty fields with a named reason.

acceptance.intent: A valid submission returns 201 with the stored book's title and author.
An empty title returns 400 and names the title field.
An empty author returns 400 and names the author field.
A whitespace-only title is treated as empty and returns 400.

nodes.summary: Remove a book and omit it from the next read; report a missing id without altering the list.
nodes.instructions:
Add DELETE /books/{id}. A stored id is removed through books.delete and returns 204.
An unknown id returns 404 and leaves the list unchanged, per AC-002.
Pytest covers the removal and the missing-id behavior.
nodes.name: Remove a book and omit it from the next read; report a missing id without altering the list.

acceptance.intent: GET /books returns status 200 with a JSON array.
Books added in sequence are listed in the order they were added.
A removed book returns status 204 and is absent from the next list read.
Removing an id that is not in the list returns 404 and leaves the list unchanged.
